prompt: A branch needs to answer all existing internal records during a temporary primary outage, using its own valid data. Which design fits?
options: A secondary holding a full zone copy
A stub holding only authority metadata
A DNS suffix on every workstation
A conditional rule pointing only to the unavailable primary
en: A valid secondary can serve its full copy without asking the failed primary for each answer.
ru: Valid secondary failed primary se har jawab poochay baghair apni full copy serve kar sakta hai.

prompt: One server is primary for lab.example and secondary for branch.example. A colleague says this is impossible. What is accurate?
options: Roles belong to individual zones, so this combination is possible
Every server must have one permanent role for all namespaces
The server must be renamed before hosting another zone
Only stub zones can share a server
en: A server may host different roles for different zones.
ru: Server mukhtalif zones ke liye mukhtalif roles host kar sakta hai.

prompt: Two writable domain-controller DNS replicas host an AD-integrated zone. Which interpretation fits?
options: They can accept suitable updates and use AD replication
The second must always be a standard read-only secondary
Every query requires a full AXFR between the replicas
Both become stubs because they are domain controllers
en: AD-integrated replication is different from standard file-backed primary/secondary replication.
ru: AD-integrated replication standard file-backed primary/secondary se alag hai.

prompt: Two DNS VMs have valid copies but share one ESXi host and its storage. What risk remains?
options: Failure of shared infrastructure may stop both
The secondary automatically runs on another physical host
DNS replication eliminates host failures
Different VM names guarantee independent recovery
en: Separate VM instances do not remove shared failure dependencies.
ru: Alag VM instances shared failure dependencies khatam nahin kartin.

prompt: You need to test DNS02 at .122 for DNS01’s name. Which command isolates that server choice?
options: nslookup dns01.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.122
nslookup dns02.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.121
nslookup dns01.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.121
nslookup dns03.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.123
en: The final address selects the resolver; the queried host name is a separate argument.
ru: Aakhri address resolver select karta hai; queried host name alag argument hai.

prompt: Output says Server: Unknown but then returns the correct host address. What is a careful conclusion?
options: Forward resolution worked; the resolver’s reverse display name may be unavailable
The correct host address must be discarded as invalid
The entire DNS system is offline
A missing PTR proves the cause of every earlier timeout
en: The resolver display name and the requested answer are separate checks.
ru: Resolver display name aur requested answer alag checks hain.

prompt: An A lookup succeeds but RDP to the returned address fails. What is the next relevant area?
options: RDP service, TCP reachability and access controls
Assume DNS success guarantees the application works
Convert the primary zone into a stub immediately
Delete the A record because any connection failure proves it is wrong
en: DNS resolves a name; it does not prove application availability.
ru: DNS naam resolve karta hai; application availability ka proof nahin.

prompt: An administrator adds DNS03’s A record on DNS01. Which additional configuration is not accomplished by that action?
options: Installing and configuring the DNS service on DNS03
Storing DNS03’s name mapping in the primary
Making the new record available for appropriate zone queries
Maintaining the new data at the writable source
en: Creating a record about a machine does not configure software on that machine.
ru: Machine ka record banana us machine par software configure nahin karta.

prompt: The alias dns.vcplab.com should lead to DNS01. What belongs in its CNAME target field?
options: dns01.vcplab.com
0.168.192.in-addr.arpa
en: CNAME references a canonical DNS name; that name’s address record supplies the IP.
ru: CNAME canonical DNS naam ko reference karta hai; us naam ka address record IP deta hai.

prompt: A host A query works, but the corresponding reverse query fails. What should be inspected?
options: The separate reverse zone and PTR data
Only the spelling of the VMware VM folder
Assume a working A record proves every PTR exists
Replace the A record with a subnet mask
en: Forward and reverse records are separate and require separate verification.
ru: Forward aur reverse records alag hain; verification bhi alag chahiye.

prompt: A new test record exists on DNS01 but is absent when querying DNS02 directly. What is the focused investigation?
options: Compare SOA serials and inspect refresh, master and transfer permissions
Rename DNS02 to the test record’s name
Clear every client cache without inspecting the secondary
Disable all DNS server interfaces
en: Direct stale results on the secondary call for zone-update diagnostics.
ru: Secondary par direct stale result zone-update diagnostics mangta hai.

prompt: Notify is enabled on DNS01. Someone marks new-record replication complete without checking DNS02. What evidence is missing?
options: The new data or relevant updated version on DNS02
The name of the Notify button
A screenshot of the Windows wallpaper
A successful lookup of an unrelated public name
en: Notify prompts checking; it is not the transfer’s completion receipt.
ru: Notify check ka signal hai; transfer completion ki receipt nahin.

prompt: DNS01 is offline for an extended period and DNS02’s secondary copy expires. What must not be assumed?
options: That DNS02 can keep serving the expired zone indefinitely
That copy validity matters for answering
That recovery needs investigation and planning
That zone expiry differs from record-cache TTL
en: An expired secondary cannot be relied on as an unlimited offline authoritative copy.
ru: Expired secondary ko unlimited offline authoritative copy nahin samjha ja sakta.

prompt: DNS03’s stub shows SOA, NS and necessary DNS01 address data but no ordinary alias list. What does that indicate?
options: A limited authority-information copy, consistent with a stub
A full secondary with all records necessarily hidden
Proof every remote authority is reachable
Automatic creation of an AD domain trust
en: The missing ordinary record list is expected for the stub model.
ru: Stub model mein ordinary record list ka na hona expected hai.

prompt: A stub answers a host lookup correctly. Which claim needs separate evidence?
options: Which upstream authority or cached data actually supplied the answer
That this query produced an answer
That the client submitted a DNS question
That the chosen resolver was contacted for the test
en: Client-visible success alone does not establish the exact resolver packet path.
ru: Client-visible success akeli exact resolver packet path establish nahin karti.

prompt: The stub’s required authorities are unreachable, and no usable answer is cached. Can it supply an arbitrary missing host record from its own full copy?
options: No; it does not hold that full ordinary record set
Yes; every stub includes a full backup invisibly
Yes; it creates an A record from the requested spelling
Yes; it returns the subnet mask as the host address
en: Authority metadata does not contain every host’s answer.
ru: Authority metadata mein har host ka answer nahin hota.

prompt: DNS01 has KRNC.org → 172.16.0.18 saved, but the isolated lab has no verified route to that subnet. What is the next prerequisite?
options: Establish the target’s real availability and a valid permitted network path
Assume the saved rule created a route
Change every local host to the remote DNS address
Delete the local authoritative zone first
en: A forwarding rule does not build routing or prove the target exists.
ru: Forwarding rule routing nahin banata aur target ka hona prove nahin karta.

prompt: A known remote name resolves directly at 172.16.0.18 but fails through DNS01. What should be examined?
options: DNS01’s matching rule, target settings and its own path/policy
Assume direct success means the target is offline
Only the client’s desktop resolution
Only the local reverse-zone capitalization
en: The forwarding server can have a different network path or policy from the direct test client.
ru: Forwarding server ka network path ya policy direct test client se alag ho sakta hai.

prompt: DNS-A sends unresolved questions for the same namespace to DNS-B, which sends them back to DNS-A. What design fault is likely?
options: A forwarding loop
A complete authoritative zone transfer
A successful signed delegation
A primary DNS suffix change
en: Circular forwarding can delay or fail resolution rather than reach an answer source.
ru: Circular forwarding answer source tak pohanchne ke bajaye resolution delay ya fail kar sakti hai.

prompt: A zone shows DNSKEY and RRSIG records after signing. What additional claim is not established by that view?
options: That a separate resolver successfully performed DNSSEC validation
That DNSSEC-related records were published
That zone signing generated signature material
That the zone view differs from its unsigned state
en: Signing and downstream validation need distinct evidence.
ru: Signing aur downstream validation ki evidence alag chahiye.

prompt: A colleague wants to copy the private KSK to a resolver as its trust anchor. What is the appropriate alternative?
options: Use authenticated public DNSKEY or DS anchor information
Share the administrator password instead
Publish the private key as a TXT record
Disable signature checking and call it validated
en: Trust-anchor distribution uses trusted public material, not private signing secrets.
ru: Trust-anchor distribution trusted public material use karti hai, private signing secrets nahin.

prompt: The classroom zone was signed and then unsigned. Which checkpoint is accurate?
options: Final state unsigned; anchor import and validation were not demonstrated
All resolvers were proven to validate every answer
All DNS traffic became encrypted permanently
The unsigned zone automatically retained active signatures
en: The record supports the signing/unsigning exercise, not full validation deployment.
ru: Record signing/unsigning exercise support karta hai, full validation deployment nahin.

prompt: DNS03 is given suffix VCPLAB.Com while retaining WORKGROUP. What changed?
options: Its naming context; AD joining was not performed
It became an AD domain controller
It gained every zone record automatically
Its static IP became a DNSKEY record
en: A suffix change is distinct from domain membership and DNS role configuration.
ru: Suffix change domain membership aur DNS role configuration se alag hai.

prompt: dns02.vcplab.com. resolves but the short name dns02 fails in an application. What is the best area to check?
options: That application/client’s suffix-search and resolution behavior
Assume the successful absolute A record is missing
Delete the primary zone immediately
Promote the secondary before any inspection
en: Absolute-name success narrows attention to short-name expansion and resolver paths.
ru: Absolute-name success short-name expansion aur resolver paths ki taraf tawajjuh lati hai.

prompt: Computer properties show DNS03.VCPLAB.Com, but DNS01 returns NXDOMAIN for that name. What should be checked?
options: Whether DNS01 hosts the required record and whether registration/creation succeeded
Treat local computer properties as proof the remote record exists
Replace the DNS suffix with the subnet mask
Assume this proves all signatures are expired
en: Local naming is not proof of matching server-side DNS data.
ru: Local naming matching server-side DNS data ka proof nahin.
